title: Example Sequencer & Provenance — Prompt Lab Notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for an example-sequencer experiment: crank through ordering of exemplars, attach lightweight provenance markers to outputs, and surface brittle example-level failure modes. Goal is to find reproducible heuristic rules for ordering / pruning that improve downstream classification stability and make failure triage easier.

Context / motivation:
- Many few-shot templates show large variance depending on which examples are included and in what order; ops for teams are: choose set, freeze order, or rely on model robustness. I want a middle ground: a sequencer that chooses and annotates exemplars with minimal cost.
- Add provenance tokens / markers so that when a model hallucinates or flips label, we can map back to the most influential exemplar candidates.

High-level hypothesis:
- Hypothesis 1: Interleaving positive/negative exemplars reduces label flipping vs grouped blocks.
- Hypothesis 2: Placing a short paraphrase exemplar immediately before the query helps anchor style and reduces hallucinated attributes.
- Hypothesis 3: Small provenance suffix (e.g., "[ex#3]") appended to each exemplar in the prompt allows cheap downstream attribution via token-level attention / saliency heuristics.

Quick experiment matrix (local harness):
- Variables: shots = {2,4,8}; ordering = {grouped, interleaved, similarity-ranked}; provenance = {none, bracket-id, natural-language-sentinel}; model = {redwood-open-1-7b, redwood-open-13b-quant}.
- Metrics: label-accuracy, flip-rate across 5 reruns (seeded), average response token length, % of responses with provenance echo.
- Run command (dev box):
  python eval/run_sequencer.py --shots 4 --ordering interleaved --prov bracket-id --model redwood-open-1-7b --out results/seq-4-int-bracket.json

Example prompt templates (working drafts) — little snippets for quick paste/testing:
- Template A (interleaved, bracket ids):
  System: You are an assistant that responds with a single label: POSITIVE, NEGATIVE, or NEUTRAL. Do not add anything else.
  EX1: Review: "Terrible service, food cold." Label: NEGATIVE [ex#1]
  EX2: Review: "Had a nice quiet dinner, staff attentive." Label: POSITIVE [ex#2]
  EX3: Review: "Food was okay, nothing special." Label: NEUTRAL [ex#3]
  Query: "Dinner was cold, but the waiter was friendly." Label:

- Template B (similarity-ranked, prose provenance):
  System: Short label only: POSITIVE / NEGATIVE / NEUTRAL. Each example ends with a provenance tag in parentheses indicating source ID.
  EX1: "The app crashed halfway through checkout." => NEGATIVE (src:usr-142)
  EX2: "Checkout was smooth, no issues." => POSITIVE (src:usr-87)
  EX3: "Payment page slow but succeeded." => NEUTRAL (src:usr-55)
  Query: "Abandoned payment, then came back and it worked." =>

Failure modes I want to capture / reproduce:
- Provenance echo contamination: model repeats bracket token but assigns it to wrong exemplar in explanation.
- Token-budget collapse: after ~8 shots, model truncates provenance markers (they get cut mid-tag), making attribution noisy.
- Style bleed: exemplar style (exclamations, emojis) causes query to adopt sentiment intensity bias.
- Adversarial exemplar: a single outlier exemplar with strong lexical cues flips majority.

Quick notes from yesterday's run (raw, unfiltered):
- 4-shot interleaved + bracket-id reduced flip-rate from ~0.23 -> ~0.14 on dataset X-small.
- However, bracket-id echoed verbatim in ~42% of responses for 1-7b (annoying). Might be useful for parsing but also pollutes output when we want only labels.
- Similarity-ranked ordering gave marginal gains for NEUTRAL class recall.
- 13b-quant was less likely to echo explicit bracket ids but showed higher hallucination of attributes.

Attribution heuristics I'm prototyping:
- Simple token-count: count occurrences of each exemplar-id token in the generation. Choose exemplar with highest count as "influencer". Fast but brittle.
- Delta-probing: rerun the prompt with each exemplar removed and measure change in logprob for the chosen label. Expensive but cleaner.
- KV-backtrace (if we can get attention maps from serving runtime): map high-attn spans to exemplar boundaries. Requires additional infra hooks in Redwood Private/Dedicated.

Small set of few-shot exemplars to keep around (seed bank):
- T1: "Ordered item missing, no response from support." => NEGATIVE [ex-miss1]
- T2: "Quick delivery, as promised." => POSITIVE [ex-speed1]
- T3: "Product matched description but packaging dented." => NEUTRAL [ex-pack1]
- T4: "Customer support arranged refund promptly." => POSITIVE [ex-refund1]

Ad-hoc testing checklist before labeling a new template as 'stable':
- Run 10 seeded trials, measure flip-rate <= 0.12 for target dataset
- Confirm provenance markers do not appear in >5% of clean label-only responses (postprocess removal OK but prefer they not be generated)
- Memory: average tokens per request < 1024 for cost target
- Evaluate on one adversarial perturbed query per class

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Q: Is bracket-id the simplest path or do we prefer natural-language provenance so model treats it as context not instruction?
- TODO: Add a compact parser to strip provenance echoes without breaking label-only outputs (regex-based first pass).
- TODO: Push small KV-backtrace spike to infra to test on Dedicated cluster. Open ticket: CON-1423.
- TODO: Check if rollout to redwood-dedicated 13b quant is feasible; ask infra for a 2-hour slot.
- TODO: Add a negative-sampling step to the sequencer that intentionally inserts near-duplicate counterexamples to expose brittle boundary cases.

Random thoughts / heuristics I've noticed:
- Short paraphrase exemplars immediately before query reduce hallucinated new attributes (maybe because the LM locks on lexical anchors).
- Ordering by chronological timestamp of source data sometimes helps for temporal tasks, but hurts for static label tasks. Keep it toggleable.
- When provenance token is alphanumeric-only (ex123) it's more likely to be echoed than when wrapped in brackets or parentheses.

Quick link map / references:
- ticket: CON-1423 (KV-backtrace prototype)
- GH PR: prompt-tools/pull/88 (sequencer shim)
- slack thread: #prompt-experiments (search "provenance echo")

If I lose this file in mid-edit: copy into confluence page "prompt-provenance/notes" and tag Maya.

---- end of this scratchpad entry ----

(Notes are messy — intended as a working brain dump. Will synthesize into a proper experiment plan once the bracket-id echo issue is better understood.)
